findings.frozenSummary: Two current unit tests fail and coverage cannot complete
findings.impact: The legacy Storybook gate was repaired, but the current browser-project Storybook command still fails the Compact320 interaction when the open control has no aria-controls value.

closure.expected: Make both governed and developer component-test commands green, then capture one immutable full-gate result at the candidate revision.

findings.note: Reproduced locally at the comparison source: the three selected story files ran 30 tests with 29 passing and Compact320 failing at the aria-controls assertion. The repository documents the legacy runner as authoritative, so this is an honest developer-gate defect rather than proof that the hosted merge gate is red.

findings.frozenSummary: Event catalogue, schema registry, producer wiring, consumer registration, and runtime reachability disagree

closure.expected: Compare the complete governed catalogue with an observed boot registry and make producer, schema, consumer, durability, and reachability classifications agree.

findings.note: Catalogue coverage has expanded materially, but the current checker still discovers jobs, consumers, and schedules from source syntax rather than an observed runtime registry.

findings.frozenSummary: Boundary enforcement accepts known-invalid imports in build/composition/outbox files

findings.note: The lint command now runs the in-memory negative controls; the focused checker was also executed successfully during this revalidation.

findings.frozenSummary: Dashboard and Badge bypass the governed Metric read path
findings.impact: Dashboard remains active and reads raw metric rows without definition-version, consumer-permission, or correction semantics; Badge retains the same bypass behind a dark capability.

closure.expected: Route active Dashboard reads through the governed Metric authority and either contract or remove the dark Badge reader under REC-01.

findings.note: The Badge file is byte-identical to the frozen source; Dashboard changed window semantics but retained the raw metric aggregate.

findings.frozenSummary: OAuth/JWKS/token/revoke and other Google adapters use direct `fetch` despite ADR-0050's approved gateway rule
findings.impact: Production now refuses direct credential calls, but the adapter still implements direct OAuth/JWKS/token/revoke transport and no credential-gateway implementation replaces it, so production OAuth readiness depends on unresolved wiring.

closure.expected: Route every retained production Google credential operation through the approved typed gateway/admission path and remove or structurally isolate direct production transports.

findings.note: The new guard is a valuable containment: credential-bearing direct calls always throw in production. It does not make the ADR implementation complete, and fixed-origin JWKS remains a direct read in the adapter.

findings.frozenSummary: ADR-0045's tamper-evident audit store is not implemented

closure.expected: ADR 0056 supersedes the unsupported integrity claim and executable language checks prevent Recent Activity from being presented as tamper-evident audit history.

findings.note: This closes only the frozen decision contradiction. Operational Action History remains a separate incomplete product obligation and no cryptographic integrity claim is made.
